# Workflow compatibility

<!-- Generated by tools/ci/src/gen-compatibility.ts from the parser's support matrix and the workflow corpus. Do not edit: UPDATE_COMPATIBILITY=1 pnpm --filter @fyrden/ci-tools test compatibility-doc rewrites it. -->

Which GitHub Actions workflow features Fyrden accepts, and what shows each one works. Every key and value GitHub documents is listed; a key not listed is refused as unknown, and an unsupported one is refused with the reason below.

## How each feature is shown

- **runs**: a workflow in the corpus (`packages/testing/src/ci-corpus/`) runs on the pinned runners below and its outcome is checked through the REST API. The nightly workflow runs every such case on both runner versions ([runs](https://github.com/nabobery/fyrden/actions/workflows/nightly.yml)), and pull requests that change the corpus or the runner paths run them on the newer one.
- **tested**: an existing test named in the row shows the behaviour, because it is decided by the forge before any runner is involved.
- **parsed**: the parser accepts and models it, checked on every pull request; the row says why the runner tier shows no more.

## Versions

- gitea/runner: `6.0.0`, `5.4.1`, each binary pinned by SHA-256.
- `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1` (v7.0.1)
- `actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9` (v6.1.0)
- `actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830` (v4.3.0)
- job image: `node:24@sha256:49f7adaf9f1574bc45c20ea317139b39a59d7e758d0e93745e112fd85cb42623`
- service image: `redis:7-alpine@sha256:7f7d30b7fdd09467bac58198a1f166dd69789d348d4fe859cccb20e0cf287fbe`
- dockerStep image: `busybox:1.37@sha256:a7dbc319b1438115a207e11930dc4bb3e643dcb3ec0bdd694bb36cd8fad289ec`

## YAML

| Feature | Status | Shown | By, or why not |
|---|---|---|---|
| `yaml.anchors` | supported | runs | `expressions` |
| `yaml.merge-keys` | unsupported | — | Merge keys (`<<`) are not part of YAML 1.2. Repeat the keys, or alias a whole value. |
| `yaml.tags` | unsupported | — | Workflow files do not use YAML tags. Remove the tag. |
| `yaml.directives` | unsupported | — | Workflow files are YAML 1.2; only `%YAML 1.2` is accepted as a directive. |

## Jobs

| Feature | Status | Shown | By, or why not |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobs.<job_id>.name` | supported | runs | `matrix` |
| `jobs.<job_id>.permissions` | supported | parsed | `job-fields`. What a widened job token may do is not built yet; the parser models the scopes. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.needs` | supported | runs | `needs-and-outputs` |
| `jobs.<job_id>.if` | supported | runs | `failure-and-conditions` |
| `jobs.<job_id>.runs-on` | supported | runs | `run-steps` |
| `jobs.<job_id>.runs-on.labels` | supported | parsed | `job-fields`. Label matching is the scheduler's, before any runner; the parser models the list form. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.runs-on.group` | unsupported | — | Fyrden has no runner groups; select runners by labels. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.snapshot` | unsupported | — | Fyrden does not make runner images from jobs. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.environment` | unsupported | — | Fyrden has no deployment environments yet. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency` | supported | tested | `apps/api/test/run.concurrency.test.ts`. A concurrency group is decided by the run engine before any runner is offered a job. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency.group` | supported | tested | `apps/api/test/run.concurrency.test.ts`. A concurrency group is decided by the run engine before any runner is offered a job. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency.cancel-in-progress` | supported | tested | `apps/api/test/run.concurrency.test.ts`. A concurrency group is decided by the run engine before any runner is offered a job. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency.queue` | unsupported | — | Fyrden keeps at most one pending job per group; remove `queue`. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.cache-mode` | unsupported | — | Fyrden has no shared Actions cache yet; caches stay on the runner. |
| `jobs.<job_id>.outputs` | supported | runs | `needs-and-outputs` |
| `jobs.<job_id>.env` | supported | runs | `run-steps` |

| `jobs.<job_id>.steps` | supported | runs | `run-steps` |

| `jobs.<job_id>.strategy.matrix.include` | supported | runs | `matrix` |

## Known differences

- **Actions stored on the forge** are not resolved yet: `owner/repo@ref` always names a repository on github.com. Use `./path` after `actions/checkout` for an action in the same repository.
- **Action references** keep GitHub's grammar: `owner/repo[/path]@ref`, `./path` and `docker://image`. Absolute URLs are refused.
- **`$/path`** is refused, although GitHub.com runs it as an action in the same repository at the running commit (GitHub Enterprise Server does not support it; verified in [GitHub's documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/find-and-customize-actions#adding-an-action-from-the-same-repository), 2026-11-28). Use `./path` after `actions/checkout`.
- The refusal covers references written in the workflow, not references inside the composite actions it uses: the runner reads those, and accepts its own forms there.
- **The Actions cache** lives on each runner, in the runner's own cache server; there is no cache shared between runners yet. The corpus checks save and restore with `actions/cache` v6.1.0 and v4.3.0 on a runner with its cache on, and that a restore with the cache off restores nothing and does not fail (measured with both pinned runner versions, 2026-11-28). Operators turn the cache off on runners that take public or fork jobs (`docs/ci/runners.md`).
- **Artifacts** are not served yet: nothing in the forge answers `actions/upload-artifact` or `actions/download-artifact`.
